title: Plan D review: accepted-but-unwired query scope filters + API merge/split not wired to Resolver
body:
Review of TASK-universal-media-decomposer-D-resolution-query-api (Round 1). Two cross-cutting patterns worth recording:

1. PLANNING_GAP (contract silence): StructuredQuery declares continuity_id/temporal_from/temporal_to/spatial, the /v1/query/structured router accepts and forwards them, but NO handler applies them — _temporal_conditions() returns [], _spatial_meta() returns a note. Client-supplied continuity/temporal/spatial scope is silently ignored (results unfiltered). CONTRACTS lists these filters. Wiring the scope conditions (or explicitly rejecting unsupported filters with 422) must land or the check never reopens.

2. API merge/split thickness: routers/entities.py calls SemanticCommandService.entity_resolve which ONLY appends an EntityResolved ledger event. It does NOT invoke the P1 Resolver/PostgresSplitEnumerator, so the reversible split machinery (mention rebinding, ReferenceRebound emission, ambiguity quarantine) is NOT reachable through the v1 REST boundary — it exists and is tested only at the service layer. build_context does not wire the Resolver. Confirm desired v1 semantics before closing.

3. Secondary: GET /segments/{id}/evidence passes segment_id to source-scoped get_by_source() (always wrong/empty entity) — stub. No v1 route writes projection stores (P2 invariant proven); honest gating of splink/vecalign/pgvector-HNSW confirmed real, none fabricated active.

title: Plan E round 1: packaging-seam honesty bugs recur in build artifacts, static tests blind to them
body: Plan E review (TASK-universal-media-decomposer-E) found two real packaging/ops defects that no static or conditional test can catch: (1) deploy/compose.yaml:104 uses $${HATCHET_VERSION:-v0.50.0} (double-$), which compose renders as a literal ${...} — invalid image reference at pull time; the static secret test passes because '$${' contains '${'. (2) deploy/docker-entrypoint.sh:17 mask ${UMD_POSTGRES_DSN%%@*@*} needs TWO '@' in a DSN; standard DSNs have one, so the full DSN incl. password is echoed to stdout on migration-enabled startup. Both were introduced in the exact seams (compose interpolation, shell parameter expansion) that are validated only statically or by conditional Docker tests that skip here. Recommendation for future plans: review feedback loop must include shell/YAML interpolation semantics checks for deploy artifacts, not only Python lint; consider an ast-free greplint for '\$\$' in compose and for parameter-expansion masking patterns in entrypoints.

title: Discovery: deploy surface env-var naming breaks documented deployment (Plan E R2)
body: TASK-universal-media-decomposer-E round 2: src/umd/config.py Settings uses env_prefix="UMD_" + env_nested_delimiter="__" so nested settings REQUIRE double-underscore names (UMD_POSTGRES__DSN, UMD_OCFL__ROOT, UMD_PROJECTION__VECTOR_HNSW_MIN_VERSION). The entire deploy surface uses single-underscore names that pydantic-settings silently ignores: deploy/compose.yaml:23-24,29; .env.example:16,18-19,24,26; deploy/docker-entrypoint.sh:22; tests/test_api_contract.py:709. Consequence: shipped docker compose cannot connect API->db (defaults to 127.0.0.1 inside container) and bypasses the /data/ocfl named volume; tests/test_api_contract.py::test_app_factory_builds_wired_app_over_real_postgres fails in a clean env and silently passes against the WRONG (default) database whenever a pre-migrated `umd` db exists — masking the defect in earlier rounds. Also: README.md:9-10,34 claims 380 passing/2 skipped; actual 411 collected = 406 passed + 4 skipped + 1 failed. README.md:124 says 22 tables; actual 23. Fix: rename env vars to `__` form (config is authoritative per docs/deployment.md:44-45) and fix the test monkeypatch; update README counts. Category: discovery + tag needsreview.

title: Plan F migration 0006 GUC widen — defense-in-depth note
body: Migration 0006 (umd.projection_wipe='vector' GUC opt-in for EmbeddingProjectionBuilder.wipe) does NOT weaken the immutable-embedding guarantee under the test: test_embedding_is_append_only and test_embedding_immutable_supersession_never_deletes still raise on non-builder UPDATE/DELETE (both green in 469/4/0 run). The GUC is transaction-scoped (set_config is_local=true) and consistent between vector.py:104 and the migration docstring. One defense-in-depth nuance: the block_embedding_mutate trigger trusts ANY caller that sets the GUC — it does not verify the caller is the builder/single-writer. Acceptable within the documented trust model (single app role, parameterized SQL, no injection), but if a future code path reuses the GUC name, it could DELETE embeddings. Recommend a hard session/set-role marker or trigger-side caller check as future hardening. Non-blocking. tagged uncertainty; verdict PASS.

title: Plan I Round 3: PLANNING_GAP — ready line after blocking start() is unobservable on pinned SDK; probe always times out
body:
TASK-universal-media-decomposer-I-hatchet-worker-integration Round 3 final fresh review. Gates: ruff clean; mypy --strict clean (9 Plan I files); mypy --strict tests/test_hatchet_live.py = exactly 1 PRE-EXISTING error (line 303 hatchet_sdk import-not-found, GATED uninstalled dep) — not introduced by Round 2. UMD_TEST_POSTGRES=true pytest tests/test_hatchet_live.py = 27 passed / 3 honest cluster skips (exact match to documented state). Round-2 findings verified: F2 stale handoff §3 rewritten (REQUIRED 'grep worker started:' block removed; Plan-J-do-not-treat-as-evidence note added) ✓ FIXED; F3 two stale test docstrings corrected (module marking semantics lines 22-31; test_no_fake_gated_ready_claim lines 1163-1168) ✓ FIXED. F1 (real-SDK worker loop start) FIXED mechanically: cli.py:131 client.worker("umd-worker", workflows=handle.registered_workflows); :132 worker.start() exactly once; factory collects registered_workflows in BOTH branches (hatchet.py:388-424,435-441); structural test test_sdk_worker_contract_registers_workflows_and_starts_once (test line 1223) asserts non-empty registrations / worker args / exactly-once start / exact ready-line string — verified against pinned wheel hatchet_sdk-1.38.1 (/tmp/hatchet-check): Hatchet.worker is a method (hatchet.py:265), Worker.start() exists (worker/worker.py:402), ClientConfig(token, host_port) — no api_url/token kwargs (config.py:215-226), task(name=) keyword-only returning Standalone, runs.admin_client().run_workflow(wf_name, str input) (features/runs.py:150, clients/admin.py:414).

NEW PLANNING_GAP (the plan contract is the defective party): cli.py prints worker_ready_line ONLY after worker.start() returns (P2-S3 Decision B / QA R2 amendment text 'emit readiness only after that call returns'). Verified against the pinned wheel: Worker.start() calls self._loop.run_forever() (BLOCKS for the worker's entire healthy lifetime) then `if self._handle_kill: sys.exit(0)` (handle_kill defaults True, worker/worker.py:97,435). Therefore cli.py:138 print(worker_ready_line(...)) is UNREACHABLE in every scenario: healthy run -> blocked in run_forever; SIGTERM shutdown -> SystemExit(0) raised INSIDE start() before the print; SIGKILL -> no chance. wait-for-worker.sh:35 greps 'worker ready: registered' which can never appear in the worker log -> the probe ALWAYS times out (240s) on a healthy stack -> Plan J's hosted workflow fails on a correctly-running stack. This is exactly the stale-probe failure the handoff §3 warns about ('a stale probe would always time out on a correctly-running stack'), now self-inflicted by the post-start print ordering. Handoff §3 + P4-S3 'Correction' annotation both claim the ready line 'matches' the probe and tell Plan J not to change it — false on the pinned SDK. Fix (planner): emit worker_ready_line AFTER the is_ready() gate + client.worker(...) construction and IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the blocking worker.start() (start() still validates actions non-empty and raises ValueError -> non-zero exit -> probe's exited-state + log-dump path catches it, so readiness stays honest: process either stays alive in the loop or exits non-zero). Strengthen the structural test to assert the ready line precedes the blocking start call. Correct handoff §3 + P4-S3 annotation accordingly. DocsGenerator/TestGenerator not spawned (concurrent sessions own shared files; inline-equivalent evidence used, same standard as prior rounds). Log-only: worker_ready_line count = len(work_registry) vs len(registered_workflows) (equal only when registration complete; contextlib.suppress in factory could mask silent registration loss); cli.py imports umd.api.app engine_from_settings (composition root, pre-existing pattern); compose.yaml hatchet comment says 'build gate' but lacks explicit CANDIDATE/PENDING wording (runtime.txt/pyproject/handoff carry it). Verdict: ISSUES_FOUND (PLANNING_GAP x1, release-gate-blocking, route amend plan).
